segments.title: Saskatoon Police Service 2025 Business Plan Presentation
segments.takeaway: The Saskatoon Police Service presented its 2025 Business Plan, outlining strategic themes including community safety, staffing, partnerships, and innovation for the upcoming year.

segments.title: Improving Reporting Systems and Next-Gen 911
segments.takeaway: The committee discussed plans to enhance online reporting and the transition to Next Generation 911, which will eventually include texting options, with an estimated implementation by 2028-2029.

segments.title: Addressing Language Barriers with Technology
segments.takeaway: The committee inquired about technology to overcome language barriers, learning about "Language in Motion" for officers and future body camera translation capabilities.

segments.title: Measuring Community Safety and Public Perception
segments.takeaway: The committee discussed plans for an annual public perception survey to measure the community's feeling of safety and benchmark the effectiveness of implemented strategies.

segments.title: Warrant Enforcement and Intimate Partner Violence Program
segments.takeaway: The committee discussed the police service's warrant enforcement strategy in relation to the new Marshals and the proactive, community-based approach of the Intimate Partner Violence team.

segments.title: Citywide Safety Plan and Data-Driven Traffic Safety
segments.takeaway: The committee inquired about the citywide safety plan's community engagement and the data-driven approach to traffic safety, emphasizing continuous monitoring and balancing enforcement efforts.

segments.title: Acceptance of Business Plan Report
segments.takeaway: The committee moved to accept the Saskatoon Police Service 2025 Business Plan report following the presentation and question period.

segments.title: Update on Treaty and Reconciliation Implementation Plan
segments.takeaway: The committee received an update on the Treaty and Reconciliation Implementation Plan, detailing policy reforms, indigenous procurement, cultural events, and training for new recruits.
